narrative:
##SUMMARY##
US policy rates remain steady as the Fed Funds Rate held at 3.88 percent. Treasury yields nudged higher, with the 10-year benchmark at 5.31 percent. The Federal Reserve's balance sheet slipped to 6.74 trillion dollars. The overnight reverse repo facility expanded to 1.5 billion dollars. Overall market liquidity appears modestly tighter.

##FRESH:fed_funds_rate##
The Fed Funds Rate stayed at 3.88 percent on October 5. The level matches the prior reading. No change was reported. Policy remains unchanged.

##FRESH:treasury_10y##
The 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.31 percent on October 5. This is up 0.07 percentage points from the previous period. The increase signals a modest move higher. Yield levels are now above five percent.

##FRESH:fed_balance_sheet##
The Fed's balance sheet fell to 6.74 trillion dollars as of September 30. This represents a decline of 4.7 billion dollars from the prior period. The reduction reflects a slight contraction. The balance sheet now sits below seven trillion.

##FRESH:reverse_repo##
The overnight reverse repo facility rose to 1.5 billion dollars on October 2. This is an increase of 0.9 billion dollars from the previous reading. The jump indicates more usage of the facility. Liquidity support grew in the latest week.

##RECENT##
US GDP stands at 24,408.011 billion dollars. The CPI sits at 334.131 and core CPI at 337.765. PCE index is 131.579 while nonfarm payrolls total 159,044 thousand jobs. Unemployment is 4.2 percent and manufacturing employment is 12,652 thousand jobs. BIS cross-border credit totals 21,552.863 billion dollars, IMF world GDP growth is 2.028 percent, and the ECB deposit rate is 2.26 percent.

##WATCH##
Markets will watch the Federal Reserve's next policy meeting for any rate adjustment. Treasury yields will be monitored for further movement. The size of the reverse repo facility will be observed for signs of liquidity shifts.
